methods.label: Replace the stars with fractions
methods.explanation:
Replace each \(n^\ast\) by \(1/n\), then check the four equalities using ordinary fraction operations. Every starred input is nonzero, so all the reciprocals are defined.

For (i), use a common denominator:
\[
\frac13+\frac16=\frac26+\frac16=\frac12\ne\frac19.
\]
Thus (i) is false.

For (ii), use twelfths:
\[
\frac16-\frac14=\frac2{12}-\frac3{12}=-\frac1{12}\ne\frac12.
\]
Thus (ii) is false.

For (iii), multiply numerators and denominators:
\[
\frac12\cdot\frac16=\frac1{12}=12^\ast.
\]
Thus (iii) is true.

For (iv), the divisor \(2^\ast=1/2\) is nonzero. Dividing by it means multiplying by its reciprocal:
\[
\frac1{10}\div\frac12=\frac1{10}\cdot2=\frac15=5^\ast.
\]
Thus (iv) is true. Exactly \(2\) statements are true, choice C.
